title: Optimistic-ACK and graceful-degrade patterns for Python streaming chat SDK
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: reduce end-user latency and perceived failures for streaming chat completions by introducing an "optimistic-ack" surface and a deterministic graceful-degrade path. This ticket captures design, API changes, telemetry needs, and implementation tasks for the Python SDK.
background: Customers building conversational UX see poor perceived reliability when partial streaming fragments are lost or when server-side capacity pressure triggers abrupt stream termination. Previous approaches either block until final completion or force expensive retries. We need an ergonomics-first design that: (1) lets app code consume incremental events safely, (2) provides an opinionated ACK/commit semantic so we can garbage-collect or checkpoint progress, and (3) falls back to a non-streaming completion when streaming cannot meet latency/SLOs.
proposal: Introduce a SoftAck token and 'optimistic_ack' flag on Chat.stream() that lets caller mark visible fragments as consumed. Runtime semantics: SDK emits typed events (token_delta, partial_choice, metadata, error). The caller can call event.ack() or context.ack(token) to indicate application-level acceptance. If the stream disconnects unexpectedly, SDK offers a deterministic resume token; if resumption is impossible, SDK will transparently attempt a non-streaming completion with the last-ack checkpoint as the prompt prefix. Fallthrough policy: when capacity/backpressure is detected (high queue latency or repeated transient errors), switch to fallback mode and include a special telemetry tag 'stream_fallback=graceful'.
api_changes: New surface: Chat.stream(..., optimistic_ack=True) returns an iterator of Event objects with methods: ack(), checkpoint_id() and to_dict(). Backwards compatible: existing iterator semantics unchanged unless optimistic_ack=True. Add Chat.resume(checkpoint_id) to request missing fragments from the server when supported by backend. Add ClientConfig.streaming_backoff and streaming_grace_period settings.
compatibility_tradeoffs: Pros: Lower perceived failure rate, clearer application ownership of emitted fragments, cheaper retries via resume tokens. Cons: Slightly larger event objects (checkpoint IDs), additional network roundtrip for resume in some cases, and complexity for multi-consumer fanout scenarios. We will document anti-patterns (e.g., re-ack'ing the same checkpoint across different logical consumers without coordination).
implementation_plan: 1) Add Event wrapper class with ack()/checkpoint_id() + lightweight serialization (1 day). 2) Wire optimistic_ack flag through streaming layer and persist checkpoint IDs in in-memory ring buffer (2 days). 3) Implement fallback to non-streaming completion using last checkpoint as prefix (1 day). 4) Add telemetry hooks for 'ack.latency', 'stream.queue_ms', 'stream_fallback_reason' (1 day). 5) E2E tests and deterministic replay harness (2 days). 6) Docs and migration guide (1 day).
test_plan: Unit tests for Event.ack semantics, integration test that simulates mid-stream disconnect and asserts fallback completion text contains last-ack prefix, load test to validate backpressure detection and graceful degrade within configured SLA. Add deterministic replay test using recorded checkpoint IDs.
observability: Emit metrics: sdk.stream.acks_total, sdk.stream.ack_latency_ms (histogram), sdk.stream.fallbacks_total{reason}, sdk.stream.resume_attempts_total. Attach trace spans around ack() and resume operations. Add a console dashboard tile for 'Streaming reliability' showing fallback rate, average ack latency, and top failure reasons.
telemetry_contract: Events must include: checkpoint_id (opaque string), sequence_number (int), fragment_tokens (int), final_flag (bool), stream_source (host/region). Telemetry boolean tags: optimistic_ack_enabled, fallback_triggered. Use existing telemetry pipeline; new fields are optional for older SDK versions.
security_considerations: Checkpoint IDs are opaque and must not contain PII. When Private deployment is used, we must ensure resume tokens are encrypted with the customer KMS; SDK should never log raw tokens. Marked: security_review_required=false but will add a short security checklist for Private customers.
migration_notes: Old callers that don't opt into optimistic_ack see no behavior change. Recommend gradual rollout: default optimistic_ack=False for GA; enable it via feature flag for select customers. Provide example patterns to avoid: calling ack() before rendering to user; holding ack too long (increases memory).
qa_notes: QA should run canned scenarios: stable stream, intermittent packet loss, backend capacity eviction. Verify that user-visible text equals concatenation of acknowledged fragments after resume/fallback. Validate telemetry tags and that fallback rate remains below 0.5% on canary.
acceptance_criteria:
- Event.ack() API implemented and documented.
- Mid-stream disconnect results in either resume (if server supports) or non-streaming completion using last-ack prefix.
- Telemetry emitted for ack latency and fallback reason.
- Unit and integration tests pass in CI.
- Feature gated behind 'optimistic_ack' and opt-in for GA rollout.
notes:
Sample usage pattern (for docs):

from redwood import Chat

chat = Chat()
for evt in chat.stream(prompt, optimistic_ack=True):
    if evt.type == 'token_delta':
        # render incremental tokens to UI
        ui.append(evt.text)
        # once rendered and user visible, ack so SDK can checkpoint
        evt.ack()
    if evt.type == 'error':
        # determines whether to attempt resume or fallback
        logger.warn('stream error', evt.error)
        # application can call chat.resume(evt.checkpoint_id) or rely on SDK fallback

When implementing, keep the Event.keep_small() principle: checkpoint IDs are short base64 strings and fragments are incremental deltas.
